capabilities: Automatically track time spent on each note without timers
Split active time into reading versus writing with a heuristic
Roll up time by folder tree from topic to subfolder to file
Visualize attention as heatmap, rankings, calendar, and word trend charts
Export every chart to PNG, JSON, or CSV
extras: Data is stored as append-only JSONL files in a .mindtrace/ folder inside the vault; the README states no network, telemetry, or note content is read. A Chinese-language version of the docs is also available.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to see how much time you spend reading or writing each note or topic over days and weeks.
summary: Local-first attention tracker that silently logs time spent per note and visualizes it as topic x time dashboards, streaks, and word trends.
